items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: My first ‘78 I ever bought was Lester Young, “Sometimes I’m Happy” and “Afternoon of a Basie-ite” on Keynote with Johnny Guarnieri and Slam Stewart.

ctx.x: I hear some Lester Young in what you play. Am I off the mark with that?

No certainly not. Lester is I think my favorite clarinet player and a great composer and great tenor player. My first ‘78 I ever bought was Lester Young, “Sometimes I’m Happy” and “Afternoon of a Basie-ite” on Keynote with Johnny Guarnieri and Slam Stewart. And I was just telling Phil Atterbury from the Mississippi Rag that I met Slam Stewart in a club in Annapolis, Maryland and I went up and I said, “You know I’ve have this great record that you’re on and it meant so much to me through the years.” And he says,…
You had a pretty good experience in high school and so forth with jazz?
